prerequisites: Basic training modules (common to industrial branch and specific electrical technology)
Transmission and Distribution of Electrical Energy
Management and Operation of Electrical Power Systems

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge about control of electrical machines and drives and their applications.
Ability to calculate and design low and medium voltage electrical installations.
Ability to calculate and design high voltage electrical installations.
Ability to calculate and design electrical lines and electrical energy transmission.
Knowledge about power electrical systems and their applications.

Describe and explain the basic principles governing the automation of distribution networks, their relationship with the improvement of quality and continuity of electricity supply and the need to develop new methods of operating these networks.

Recognize, select, analyze and design the signal acquisition, processing and transmission systems involved in the automation and control of medium voltage distribution as well as their protection systems. Recognize, analyze and design the methodologies and techniques involved in efficient distribution management: demand management, losses, service quality, fault detection and location, and service restoration.
Properly handle specific computer programs for simulating electrical power systems for monitoring and controlling distribution networks and the communication systems involved.
Select and apply the legislation and regulations that electrical grids and equipment involved in automated distribution network operation must comply with.

syllabus_topics: Automation of distribution and smart grids
Distribution management and demand management systems
Interruption management: legal regulations for individual and zonal supply cut records
Protection of HV and MV smart grids
Fault location based on oscillographic records
Characteristics of electricity distribution in LV
Smart metering and remote management systems: architecture, features
Synergies with real-time network operation: interconnection strategies with SCADA/DMS systems, functionalities and synergies
Real-time management of a network with a high index of Distributed Generation: Self-consumption and Self-producers, applicable technical legislation and energy management
Control of distributed energy resources interconnected by power electronic converters
Wireless communication: Wimax, Vsat, Digital Radio
Process or Telecontrol networks: topology, systems, concepts
IEEE 1547 Standard (Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources) and IEC 61850 Standard Protocol (substation automation)
Scope of standards: concepts, versions, evolution
Operating modes of distributed energy resources
Communication protocols supported by IEEE 1547 standard
Interoperability between different manufacturers for IEC61850 standard: keys
Real applications: most important functions serving smart grids
teaching_methods: Expository classes (participatory master classes and board practices)
Classroom practices/seminars/workshops (example development and critical discussion)
Laboratory/field/computer classroom practices (visits to relevant facilities, practices with IEDs, Substation SCADA)
assessment_rules: For the ordinary assessment, if all established minimums are met (P1 minimum of 4 out of 10), the final grade is calculated as 0.8*P1 + 0.1*AS + 0.1*PA. Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. The extraordinary assessment consists of a practical exam covering all course content, and the grade obtained in this exam will be the final grade for this assessment.
